transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-02
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Eliot Park (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood CSM), Roger Li (MapleCrest Head of ML), Anika Bose (Platform Lead), Matt O'Brien (Procurement)

[00:00] Eliot Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check-in — happy 2 have you, um, hope this time works for timezone. we'll go 30, maybe 40, ish? agenda: top-up ask, geo-residency, and private pilot.
[00:18] Roger Li: yep that's fine. high level we've increased chat traffic 3x last quarter. currently on hosted plan, hitting throttles during eu morning. main ask is add eu + uk regions and an committed top-up for steady state and burst for campaigns.
[00:35] Samira Khan: thanks for that context, roger. curious — are you seeing latency or queueing? is it more backpressure on tokens or per-request p99 spikes?
[00:49] Anika Bose: p99 spikes mainly, especially for sequence-heavy prompts. average latency ok, but p99 creeping up to 1.8s in some EU zones, we target <1s p99 for chat. also embeddings batch jobs are noisy at midnight UTC.
[01:12] Diego Alvarez: totally get it. we've seen similar patterns with other finance customers. two levers: dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) for predictable p99, or hosted with committed burst credits and routing policies. both have tradeoffs on cost and failover.
[01:35] Roger Li: quick Q on sovereignty — regulator wants UK-only residency for certain PII-derived vectors. can we isolate UK geocluster? also needs KMS and audit logs for the pilot.
[01:52] Samira Khan: yes, we can provision a UK geocluster with data residency controls. for KMS we integrate with customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS). audit logs and per-request tokens are available in Console; Diego will run through retention and export options.
[02:10] Roger Li: cool. is there a difference in model variants across regions? we worry about fallbacks changing output quality.
[02:22] Samira Khan: great point — we support pinned model versions per rollout. fallback policy can route to a compatible quantized variant if capacity constrained, but we'll include quality evals in the pilot to ensure parity. sometimes names get mis- spelled in our tools, but we'll verify the exact model hash and quantization profile.
[02:45] Matt O'Brien: procurement question — if we move to dedicated reserved capacity, is there a minimum term? and how does burst get priced?
[02:56] Eliot Park: reserved pools are typically 12-month commits for price predictability, though we can do flexible quarter-based with slightly different pricing. burst is invoiced based on overage tiers or separate burst credits; we'll include clear numbers in the amended quote.
[03:18] Anika Bose: we wanted a short pilot first — private VPC — to validate latency and KMS before committing. what's involved?
[03:27] Samira Khan: pilot would be Redwood Private VPC with our control plane but customer network peering (or dedicated peering) depending on infra. steps: scope infra, hardware profile (GPU class), model & tokenizer set, prompt deck, monitoring hooks, and a run window for X days. we usually do a 2-week smoke + 4-week load test.
[03:50] Roger Li: for GPUs, we need to validate sequence lengths of ~2k tokens. what's recommended?
[03:56] Samira Khan: for 2k sequences with our production Llama-like family, recommend A100/RTX-A5000-class or checked quantized variants; we'll propose kernel profiles and batching configs. small but important: if you rely on long KV cache reuse, that changes memory footprint — we'll size accordingly.
[04:20] Roger Li: understood. also, our security team flagged SOC2/ISO attestation for the hosted control plane. do you have those reports?
[04:29] Diego Alvarez: yes, Redwood has SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 — we can share redacted reports via the secure portal. additionally, we support SSO/SAML and RBAC for team accounts.
[04:42] Matt O'Brien: timeline-wise procurement needs vendor form and master services agreement redlines. i can start review if you send templates. can we get that by next week?
[04:51] Eliot Park: yes we'll push the vendor legal packet and amended quote by 2026-07-06.
[05:00] Anika Bose: on benchmarks — what telemetry should we provide to make sizing accurate?
[05:07] Samira Khan: ideal: request distribution (percent chat vs embeddings), average and p99 tokens per request, sample prompt set (anonymized), and target concurrency. that lets us recommend batching window and cache policy.
[05:24] Roger Li: we can share dims — but will need to sanitize. also note that some requests have attachments + tool calls; hope that doesn't throw things off.
[05:34] Samira Khan: attachments okay — we treat tool calls as separate tokens, will include that in cost modeling.
[05:40] [Timestamp jump
[15:02] Diego Alvarez: jumping into economics — rough sketch: committed 250k tokens/month for chat with burst pool of 100k tokens for campaigns; dedicated baseline for 3 GPUs as example. this is illustrative.
[15:18] Roger Li: can you show cost per 1k tokens for hosted vs ded? we need to present to CFO.
[15:25] Eliot Park: yes — hosted with commit tends to have lower up-front vs dedicated long-term. dedicated gives lower per-token at scale but commits and infra ops considerations. I'll include three scenarios in the quote: hosted commit + burst, dedicated 12m commit, and hybrid (dedicated baseline + hosted burst).
[15:48] Anika Bose: hybrid sounds sensible for us — baseline for low-latency EU/UK and hosted for rare spikes/APAC.
[16:03] Roger Li: about fallbacks — if a region is constrained, do we route to US? regulator won't accept cross-border for certain datasets.
[16:14] Samira Khan: routing policy is configurable by tag; sensitive request types can be pinned to UK-only and will fail-open only per policy. we'll outline that in the runbook.
[16:28] Matt O'Brien: ok on legal, we'll need data processing addendum and security appendix.
[16:36] Diego Alvarez: noted. also, monitoring — our Console exposes token-level cost, per-route latency, and per-model tracing. we'll give a dashboard template for the pilot.
[16:47] [Crosstalk] Roger Li: do you support customer KMS via cloud provider KMS?
[16:52] Samira Khan: yes, we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault. for on-prem HSMs we have connectors but that needs extra project scoping.
[17:05] Anika Bose: one last technical — quantized variants sometimes change hallucination rates. how do we validate quality?
[17:13] Samira Khan: we run prompt-set A/B evals with the same prompts across variants and include automatic regression alerts. for pilot we'll run a quality regression harness and share metrics.
[17:27] Diego Alvarez: we'll include eval thresholds as pilot success criteria (latency p99 <1s in UK, embeddings within X% accuracy vs baseline, no regression >5% in key prompts).
[17:41] Roger Li: solid — procurement: if legal review goes smoothly we can sign a PO end of July.
[17:49] Matt O'Brien: yes that matches our timeline.
[17:55] Eliot Park: recap: Redwood to send amended quote + legal packet by 2026-07-06, Samira to send pilot runbook draft by 2026-07-08, Roger to share telemetry by 2026-07-09. book kickoff for week of 2026-07-13. action owners captured.
[18:12] Anika Bose: thanks all. any blockers?
[18:16] Roger Li: none at the moment, just internal signoffs.
[18:20] Diego Alvarez: we'll also provision a sandbox geocluster for a smoke test if you want — a few hours to bring up.
[18:27] Roger Li: please do, that'll help our engineers.
[18:30] Eliot Park: ok we'll schedule the smoke test and include creds. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
